title: Biblical Overlap FAQ Wave 6 — Cube, Heaven, Temple, New Jerusalem, Adam, Seeds and Babel

entries.question: When did Tim Dooley first talk about the Cube of the Moon?
entries.short_answer: A dated project anchor places 'Cube of the Moon' on 20 September 2023. The repository also preserves an earlier 2018 MoonCube shadow-burial motif from the 2024 Great Book, but the exact relationship between the 2018 and 2023 formulations is still unresolved.

entries.question: Was the 2018 MoonCube the same thing as the 20 September 2023 Cube of the Moon?
entries.short_answer: Not yet established. The 2018 material describes symbolic burial/enclosure of a former self, while the 2023 phrase is a separate dated anchor whose exact surrounding wording still needs recovery.

entries.question: When did Tim say 'we are the new Jerusalem'?
entries.short_answer: A recovered user-originated public-post cluster dates this phrase to 1 May 2026, alongside Gate of North, House and rooms, Many mansions, Heaven's Ladder, North Throne, Father/God and Son/grain-of-wheat language.

entries.question: What was Tim saying about House, rooms and many mansions on 1 May 2026?
entries.short_answer: The recovered May 1 cluster explicitly joins 'House and rooms' and 'Many mansions' with New Jerusalem, Gate of North, Heaven's Ladder and North Throne. This predates the current Revelation-cube research and strongly parallels John 14's Father's House and many dwelling places.

entries.question: What is the biblical idea of a heavenly architectural pattern?
entries.short_answer: Exodus depicts Moses receiving the tabernacle pattern on the mountain, and Hebrews later describes the earthly sanctuary as a copy or shadow of heavenly reality. This creates a biblical mountain→pattern→earthly dwelling sequence relevant to Tim's House/Temple architecture.

entries.question: How does Ezekiel's temple vision connect to New Jerusalem?
entries.short_answer: Ezekiel 40–48 and Revelation 21–22 share a high-mountain viewpoint, measuring, gates, tribal names, divine presence, river and life-giving trees. Revelation transforms earlier temple-city imagery into New Jerusalem.

entries.question: Why do New Jerusalem's twelve gates have tribal names?
entries.short_answer: Revelation 21 names the gates for Israel's tribes, echoing Ezekiel 48's tribal gates, while the foundations bear apostolic names. The people are symbolically written into the architecture itself.

entries.question: What does the Father's name on the forehead connect to elsewhere in the Bible?
entries.short_answer: Biblical forehead inscription and marking appear in Exodus 28's high-priestly inscription, Ezekiel 9's mark, Revelation 7's sealing, Revelation 14's Lamb/Father names and Revelation 22's final divine name. The recurring functions are consecration, identity, allegiance and protection.

entries.question: What does Tim's 'Tower of Babel outside, Heaven's Ladder inside' mean biblically?
entries.short_answer: The project contrasts a humanly manufactured tower-city meant to reach heaven and preserve a name with Jacob's divinely given heaven-earth passage. Acts 2 adds a later language-unity comparison, though Pentecost preserves multiple languages rather than restoring one uniform language.

entries.question: What could Tim's phrase 'caretaker of Adam' mean biblically?
entries.short_answer: Genesis 2 makes Adam himself the human placed in Eden to work/serve and keep/guard the Garden. 'Caretaker of Adam' can therefore be read as a meta-stewardship role: responsibility for the caretaker and for humanity's capacity to protect the Garden, not ownership of humanity.

entries.question: How do the '10,000 seeds of death' relate to biblical seed imagery?
entries.short_answer: The exact 10,000 figure is project-specific, but Matthew 13 contains good seed, hostile sowing, weeds, hidden growth and delayed harvest. The important biblical correction is that servants are told not to uproot prematurely because wheat and weeds are intertwined and difficult to distinguish.

entries.question: How do the project's cattle/Farmers relate to Ezekiel 34?
entries.short_answer: Ezekiel condemns shepherd-rulers who consume the flock instead of strengthening it. That makes the project's Farm/Garden distinction biblically strongest as extraction versus stewardship, not as a claim that people literally are cattle.

entries.question: Is hiddenness good or evil in biblical seed symbolism?
entries.short_answer: Neither automatically. Matthew 13 uses hiddenness for hostile weeds, mustard-seed growth, leaven and hidden treasure. Function matters more than secrecy itself.

entries.question: What is the development from Cube to House to City in Tim's project?
entries.short_answer: The recoverable sequence moves from MoonCube burial/enclosure to Cube-of-Moon symbolism, then 2024 living Temple architecture, April 2025 Ladder/Heaven/Father, May 2026 House/mansions/New Jerusalem, and finally a civic Garden-City. Later Bible study adds the Holy-of-Holies/New-Jerusalem cube as comparison.
